name: Question 5
problem: Find the points of intersection of the parabola ${y}^{2}=-5(x-10)$ with the $y$-axis.
worked_solution:
When the parabola intersects the $y$-axis, we must have $x=0.$ So, we set $x=0$ and solve the resulting equation for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2} & =-5(0-10) \\ {y}^{2} & =50 \\ y & =\pm \sqrt{50} \\ y & =\pm 5\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parabola intersects the $y$-axis at $(0,5\sqrt{2})$ and $(0,-5\sqrt{2}).$

Question 5
?

Find the points of intersection of the parabola y2=−5(x−10) with the y-axis.

a
(0,52) and (0,−52)
b
(0,55) and (0,−55)
c
(0,22) and (0,−22)
d
(0,25) and (0,−25)
e
(52,0) and (−52,0)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

When the parabola intersects the y-axis, we must have x=0. So, we set x=0 and solve the resulting equation for y:

y2=−5(0−10)y2=50y=±50y=±52

Therefore, the parabola intersects the y-axis at (0,52) and (0,−52).
